items.title: Gucci seemingly on cusp of turnaround
items.summary: UK/US trade coverage reviews Kering's H1 2026 disclosures: Gucci's Western Europe DTC sales (27% of Gucci's direct retail revenue) fell 5% in H1 and 8% in Q2, still pressured by an absence of Asian and Middle Eastern tourist spending, even as group-level comparable decline narrowed to 2% in Q2. Frames the European retail floor as the market still lagging North America's recovery.

items.title: Kering stock trades lower as Gucci's turnaround lifts H1 jewelry growth
items.summary: Paris-listed Kering shares slipped 0.28% to EUR57.06 on August 13 even as Gucci's Q2 revenue decline narrowed to 2% (from 8% in Q1) and the fashion/leather-goods margin gained 0.4pp. Jewelry sales rose 14% in H1, propping up the group while investors stayed cautious; US ADR lines fell further (-3.28%) the same session, suggesting international investors remain more skeptical of the Gucci story than the Paris market.

items.title: Gucci announced as Alpine title partner from 2027 season
items.summary: Official F1 coverage confirms Gucci Racing becomes Alpine's title sponsor from 2027, ending the team's partnership with BWT; livery shifts to Gucci's red-and-green house colors with a black-and-gold Gucci Racing logo. Framed as Gucci's first move into motorsport title sponsorship and part of the brand's push to reach younger, sports-adjacent European audiences beyond fashion week circuits.

items.title: F1 Gucci-Alpine sponsorship deal analysis: 'struggling brand' gambles on F1
items.summary: Motorsport-press analysis frames the ~$150M multi-year Alpine deal explicitly as a bet by a commercially struggling Gucci to 'make it cool again' via sports culture, rather than a confident marketing flex; cites skeptical F1 fan commentary on the aesthetic fit ('I dread to think what the livery is going to look like'), an outsider critical read on Gucci's brand health distinct from fashion-press coverage.

items.title: Paparazzo, Borsetto, and Giglio - the signature handbags that define every season
items.summary: Brand-owned Threads post promoting the three flagship Demna-era bag lines (Paparazzo, Borsetto, Giglio) as a coherent handbag pillar strategy. Counted for buzz/activation tracking, not public opinion; engagement metrics were not visible on the fetched listing (Threads does not surface public like/reply counts via search).

items.title: The Gucci Borsetto is quietly becoming the it-bag
items.summary: Handbag-community outlet (feeding PurseForum's active Gucci sub-board) reports the Borsetto boston-bag silhouette gaining organic traction among collectors and stylists, citing Kate Moss and Dua Lipa sightings as social proof; treated as community-opinion signal on product desirability rather than brand marketing, since PurseForum threads independently discuss resale and quality of the style.

items.title: Kering: le retour de croissance commence hors de Gucci
items.summary: French-language trade analysis notes Kering's Q2 2026 marks its first quarterly growth after twelve consecutive quarters of decline, but stresses the recovery is broader than Gucci alone: Saint Laurent returned to growth, jewelry (notably Boucheron) advanced, and eyewear stayed steadier than fashion/leather goods. Gucci's own decline narrowed to a few points versus an 8% Q1 drop; net debt fell to EUR3.3bn largely via the L'Oreal beauty divestment, and 84 stores were closed group-wide to improve network productivity -- a critical framing that Gucci is stabilizing but is no longer the group's sole growth engine.
